import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.Instances.Sphere
import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.SmoothEmbedding

/-!
# Quadrisecants of wild knots

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Quadrisecant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrisecant)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

open Manifold

namespace QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots

/-- A parametrized knot is tame if an ambient homeomorphism carries its image to the image of a
smoothly embedded circle. -/
def IsTameKnot (K : Circle → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (h : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ≃ₜ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    (f : Circle → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
    IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 1) (𝓡 3) ⊤ f ∧ h '' Set.range K = Set.range f

/-- A wild knot is a topological embedding of the circle in three-space that is not tame. -/
def IsWildKnot (K : Circle → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) : Prop :=
  Topology.IsEmbedding K ∧ ¬IsTameKnot K

/-- An affine line is a quadrisecant of `K` if it contains at least four distinct points of the
image of `K`. -/
def IsQuadrisecant (K : Circle → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    (L : AffineSubspace ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 ∧
    ∃ p : Fin 4 → Circle, Function.Injective (K ∘ p) ∧ ∀ i, K (p i) ∈ L

/-- Every wild knot in three-dimensional Euclidean space has infinitely many distinct
quadrisecant lines. -/
@[category research open, AMS 57]
theorem quadrisecants_of_wild_knots :
    ∀ K : Circle → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), IsWildKnot K →
      {L : AffineSubspace ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) | IsQuadrisecant K L}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots
modeling_decisions: Modeled the circle S¹ by Mathlib's `Circle` and ℝ³ by `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`.

Modeled a tame knot by the standard equivalent characterization that an ambient homeomorphism of ℝ³ carries its image onto the image of a smooth embedded circle. Thus a wild knot is a topological embedding that is not tame. This follows the decomposition table's PL/smooth interpretation while using Mathlib's available smooth-manifold primitives; Mathlib has no piecewise-linear knot API.

Modeled a geometric line extensionally as an `AffineSubspace ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))` whose direction has real dimension one. Consequently, infinitude means infinitely many distinct lines, not infinitely many parametrizations of lines.

Modeled 'meets the knot in at least four distinct points' using an injective map `Fin 4 → Circle` after composition with the knot map. This remains correct even if a line has infinitely many intersection points and avoids the unsuitable behavior of `Set.ncard` on infinite sets.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Quadrisecants of wild knots

A *quadrisecant* of a knot $K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ is a line that meets $K$ in at least four
distinct points. Every non-trivial tame knot has a quadrisecant (Pannwitz, Morton–Mond,
Kuperberg), and there are tame knots with only finitely many quadrisecants. It has been
conjectured that *wild* knots (knots that are not tame) always have infinitely many
quadrisecants. Kuperberg stated the conjecture for wild arcs; the Wikipedia list of unsolved
problems states it for wild knots, which is the form stated here.

A knot is *tame* if some homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries it onto a simple closed polygon
(equivalently, onto a smooth knot); otherwise it is *wild*.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Quadrisecant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrisecant)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Wild knot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_knot)
- [Ku94] Kuperberg, Greg. *Quadrisecants of knots and links*. Journal of Knot Theory and Its
  Ramifications 3 (1994), 41–50. [arXiv:math/9712205](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9712205)
-/

open Topology EuclideanGeometry

namespace QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots

/-- A line in `ℝ³`: an affine subspace whose direction is one-dimensional. -/
def IsLine (L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1

/-- A line `L` is a *quadrisecant* of a set `K ⊆ ℝ³` if it meets `K` in at least four distinct
points. -/
def IsQuadrisecant (K : Set ℝ³) (L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsLine L ∧ 4 ≤ (K ∩ L).encard

/-- A set `K ⊆ ℝ³` is a *polygonal knot* (a simple closed polygon) if it is the union of the
edges `[v i, v (i + 1)]` (indices mod `n`) of a closed polygon with `n ≥ 3` pairwise distinct
vertices `v 0, …, v (n - 1)`, where two distinct edges may only meet at a common endpoint.
In particular, adjacent edges meet exactly at their common vertex and non-adjacent edges are
disjoint. -/
def IsPolygonalKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : 3 ≤ n) (v : Fin n → ℝ³), Function.Injective v ∧
    K = ⋃ i, segment ℝ (v i) (v (finRotate n i)) ∧
    ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
      segment ℝ (v i) (v (finRotate n i)) ∩ segment ℝ (v j) (v (finRotate n j)) ⊆
        {v i, v (finRotate n i)} ∩ {v j, v (finRotate n j)}

/-- A knot `γ : Circle → ℝ³` (a topological embedding of the circle into `ℝ³`) is *tame* if some
homeomorphism of `ℝ³` carries its image onto a polygonal knot. -/
def IsTame (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, IsPolygonalKnot (h '' Set.range γ)

/-- A *wild knot* is a topological embedding `γ : Circle → ℝ³` of the circle into `ℝ³` that is
not tame, i.e. no homeomorphism of `ℝ³` carries its image onto a polygonal knot. -/
structure IsWildKnot (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : Prop where
  isEmbedding : IsEmbedding γ
  not_isTame : ¬ IsTame γ

/-- A polygonal knot is tame. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 57]
theorem isTame_of_isPolygonalKnot (γ : Circle → ℝ³) (hγ : IsPolygonalKnot (Set.range γ)) :
    IsTame γ :=
  ⟨Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, by simpa using hγ⟩

/--
**Quadrisecants of wild knots.**
It has been conjectured that wild knots always have infinitely many quadrisecants: for every
wild knot $K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ (a topological embedding of the circle that no homeomorphism
of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries onto a polygonal knot), there are infinitely many distinct lines each
meeting $K$ in at least four distinct points.

Kuperberg [Ku94] stated this conjecture for wild arcs in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The definition of a tame
knot used here is Kuperberg's: some homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries it to a piecewise
linear (equivalently, smooth) knot.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem quadrisecants_of_wild_knots (γ : Circle → ℝ³) (hγ : IsWildKnot γ) :
    {L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³ | IsQuadrisecant (Set.range γ) L}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots

The table's single-slot reading (universal statement over wild knots in ℝ³, quadrisecant = line with ≥ 4 distinct points of the knot, infinitely many distinct lines, tameness per Kuperberg) is the natural one and was followed. Note only that Kuperberg's original conjecture is for wild arcs; the Wikipedia 'wild knots' wording was formalized as instructed and the discrepancy is recorded in the docstring.
modeling_decisions: A knot is modelled as a topological embedding γ : Circle → ℝ³ (following FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/InscribedSquare.lean); quadrisecants are taken of the image set Set.range γ, so the parametrization is irrelevant.

Tameness uses Kuperberg's Definition (arXiv:math/9712205, §5): some homeomorphism h : ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³ carries the knot onto a piecewise-linear knot. The PL form was chosen over the (equivalent) smooth form to avoid manifold/immersion subtleties (a C^∞ injective non-immersive curve can be wild). A polygonal knot is made fully explicit: n ≥ 3 pairwise distinct vertices v : Fin n → ℝ³, K = ⋃ segments [v i, v (finRotate n i)], and any two distinct edges intersect only inside their common endpoints (so adjacent edges meet exactly at the shared vertex and non-adjacent edges are disjoint). Homeomorphisms of ℝ³ (rather than S³) are used, as in Kuperberg.
A wild knot is a topological embedding of the circle that is not tame (IsWildKnot as a Prop-structure with fields isEmbedding and not_isTame).

A quadrisecant of K is an affine subspace L of ℝ³ with finrank direction = 1 (idiom from ErdosProblems/209) such that 4 ≤ (K ∩ L).encard, i.e. at least four distinct points of K on the line; lines containing ≥ 5 or infinitely many points of K also count, consistent with 'at least four'. This is equivalent to Kuperberg's 'secant with two middle points'.

'Infinitely many quadrisecants' is formalized as Set.Infinite of the set of quadrisecant lines (distinct AffineSubspaces = distinct lines), per the slot notes; this is the stronger of the two possible readings (lines vs. segment-quadrisecants).
Per the decomposition table the statement is for wild knots (Wikipedia list wording), not Kuperberg's original wild arcs; the docstring records this.
Ambient space is ℝ³ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) via the repo's scoped notation; AMS tags 51 (geometry) and 57 (manifolds/knot theory).
A short proved `category test` theorem (isTame_of_isPolygonalKnot) is included as basic API for the bespoke definitions, as CONTRIBUTING.md requests.

abbrev Space := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/-- A subset of Euclidean three-space is polygonal if it is a finite union of line segments. -/
def IsPolygonal (s : Set Space) : Prop :=
  ∃ edges : Set (Space × Space), edges.Finite ∧
    s = ⋃ e ∈ edges, segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/-- A knot is tame if an ambient homeomorphism carries its image to a polygonal set. -/
def IsTameKnot (K : UnitAddCircle → Space) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : Space ≃ₜ Space, IsPolygonal (h '' Set.range K)

/-- A wild knot is a topological embedding of the circle that is not tame. -/
def IsWildKnot (K : UnitAddCircle → Space) : Prop :=
  Topology.IsEmbedding K ∧ ¬ IsTameKnot K

/-- An affine line is a quadrisecant of `K` if it contains four distinct points of its image. -/
def IsQuadrisecant (K : UnitAddCircle → Space) (L : AffineSubspace ℝ Space) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 ∧
    ∃ p : Fin 4 → Space, Function.Injective p ∧
      ∀ i, p i ∈ Set.range K ∩ (L : Set Space)

/--
Every wild knot in three-dimensional Euclidean space has infinitely many distinct
quadrisecant lines, where a quadrisecant meets the knot in at least four distinct points.
-/

    ∀ K : UnitAddCircle → Space, IsWildKnot K →

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Quadrisecants of wild knots

A *quadrisecant* of a knot $K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ is a line that meets $K$ in (at least) four
distinct points. Pannwitz, Morton–Mond and Kuperberg showed that every non-trivial *tame* knot
has a quadrisecant. Here a knot is a subset of $\mathbb{R}^3$ homeomorphic to a circle; it is
*tame* if some homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries it to a polygonal (piecewise linear)
knot, and *wild* otherwise.

It has been conjectured that every wild knot has infinitely many quadrisecants. Kuperberg's
original question is stated for wild arcs; the Wikipedia list states it for wild knots.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Quadrisecant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrisecant)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [arxiv/math/9712205](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9712205) G. Kuperberg,
  *Quadrisecants of knots and links*
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots

/-- A (topological) knot in `ℝ³`: a subset of `ℝ³` homeomorphic to the circle. -/
def IsKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (K ≃ₜ Circle)

/-- A closed polygon in `ℝ³`: the union of the line segments joining the consecutive vertices
`v 0, v 1, …, v n` and the closing segment from `v n` to `v 0`. -/
def IsClosedPolygon (S : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ³), S = ⋃ i, segment ℝ (v i) (v (i + 1))

/-- A subset `K` of `ℝ³` is *tame* if some homeomorphism of `ℝ³` carries it to a closed
polygon. For a knot `K` this is Kuperberg's definition of a tame knot. -/
def IsTame (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, IsClosedPolygon (h '' K)

/-- A *wild knot* is a knot in `ℝ³` that is not tame. -/
def IsWildKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsKnot K ∧ ¬ IsTame K

/-- The set of *quadrisecants* of `K ⊆ ℝ³`: the lines in `ℝ³` (affine subspaces whose
direction is one-dimensional) that meet `K` in at least four distinct points. -/
def quadrisecants (K : Set ℝ³) : Set (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³) :=
  {L | Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 ∧ 4 ≤ (K ∩ L).encard}

/-- A closed polygon is tame (take the identity homeomorphism). -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem IsClosedPolygon.isTame {K : Set ℝ³} (hK : IsClosedPolygon K) : IsTame K :=
  ⟨Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, by simpa using hK⟩

/-- Quadrisecants of a set are quadrisecants of any larger set. -/
@[category API, AMS 51]
theorem quadrisecants_mono {K K' : Set ℝ³} (h : K ⊆ K') :
    quadrisecants K ⊆ quadrisecants K' :=
  fun _ ⟨hL, hcard⟩ =>
    ⟨hL, hcard.trans <| Set.encard_le_encard <| Set.inter_subset_inter_left _ h⟩

/--
**Quadrisecants of wild knots.**
Every wild knot $K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ (a subset homeomorphic to a circle that no homeomorphism
of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries to a polygonal knot) has infinitely many quadrisecants, i.e. there are
infinitely many distinct lines each meeting $K$ in at least four distinct points.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem quadrisecants_of_wild_knots (K : Set ℝ³) (hK : IsWildKnot K) :
    (quadrisecants K).Infinite := by
  sorry

end QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. One remark rather than an objection: the table's 'lines meeting K in at least four distinct points' differs from Kuperberg's segment-based definition of a quadrisecant (a secant with two middle points); the table's reading was followed. Also, the statement is for wild knots while Kuperberg's original conjecture is for wild arcs; the table already notes this and the knot form was formalized.
modeling_decisions: Knot = subset of ℝ³ homeomorphic to `Circle` (Mathlib's unit circle in ℂ, compact topological space), rather than an embedding `Circle → ℝ³`; the two are equivalent since an embedding of a compact space is a homeomorphism onto its range.

Tame is defined via Kuperberg's definition with the piecewise-linear (closed polygon) form; his 'polynomial' and 'smooth' forms are classically equivalent for knots in ℝ³. Orientation-reversing homeomorphisms of ℝ³ are allowed, as in Kuperberg's definition.

`IsClosedPolygon` allows degenerate vertex data (repeated or collinear vertices, n = 0 giving a point), but since it is only applied to homeomorphic images of a knot, i.e. topological circles, the resulting sets are exactly the PL simple closed curves.

Quadrisecant is a LINE meeting K in at least four distinct points (`4 ≤ encard (K ∩ L)`), and 'infinitely many' means infinitely many distinct lines, following the decomposition table. Kuperberg's own definition counts secant segments with two middle points, under which a single line meeting K in ≥ 5 (or infinitely many) points would contribute several (or infinitely many) quadrisecants; the line-counting reading is the stronger one and is the one the table prescribes.

namespace QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots

open Set

/-- Three-dimensional Euclidean space. -/
abbrev Space := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/-- A polygonal subset of three-space is a union of finitely many closed straight segments. -/
def IsPolygonal (s : Set Space) : Prop :=
  ∃ edges : Finset (Space × Space),
    s = ⋃ e ∈ (edges : Set (Space × Space)), segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/-- A knot is tame if an ambient homeomorphism of three-space carries its image to a polygonal
subset. For an embedded circle, such a subset is a piecewise-linear knot. -/
def IsTameKnot (K : Circle → Space) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : Space ≃ₜ Space, IsPolygonal (h '' Set.range K)

/-- The set of lines that contain at least four distinct points of the image of `K`. Lines are
represented extensionally as one-dimensional affine subspaces, so different elements are distinct
lines rather than distinct parameterizations of a line. -/
def quadrisecants (K : Circle → Space) : Set (AffineSubspace ℝ Space) :=
  {L | Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 ∧
    ∃ p : Fin 4 → Space, Function.Injective p ∧
      ∀ i, p i ∈ Set.range K ∩ (L : Set Space)}

**Quadrisecants of wild knots conjecture.** Every wild knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has infinitely many
distinct quadrisecant lines. A wild knot is a topological embedding of the circle that cannot be
carried to a piecewise-linear knot by any ambient homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$; a quadrisecant
line meets the knot in at least four distinct points.
-/

theorem quadrisecants_of_wild_knots :
    ∀ (K : Circle → Space), Topology.IsEmbedding K → ¬ IsTameKnot K →
      (quadrisecants K).Infinite := by

namespace QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots

/--
A subset `S` of `ℝ³` is *polygonal* if it is a finite union of (closed) line segments.
A knot (a subset of `ℝ³` homeomorphic to a circle) which is polygonal in this sense is
exactly a polygonal knot, i.e. a simple closed polygon.
-/
def IsPolygonal (S : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : Finset (ℝ³ × ℝ³), S = ⋃ p ∈ P, segment ℝ p.1 p.2

-/
def IsTame (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, IsPolygonal (h '' K)

direction is one-dimensional) and `L` meets `K` in at least four distinct points.

def IsQuadrisecant (L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³) (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 ∧ 4 ≤ (K ∩ L).encard

theorem isQuadrisecant_of_infinite (L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³)

    IsQuadrisecant L K :=

    ¬ IsQuadrisecant L {a, b, c} := by

    refine (Set.encard_insert_le _ _).trans ?_
    refine (add_le_add_left (Set.encard_insert_le _ _) 1).trans ?_
    simp [Set.encard_singleton]; norm_num

It has been conjectured that wild knots always have infinitely many quadrisecants.

meets $K$ in at least four distinct points.

    {L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³ | IsQuadrisecant L (range γ)}.Infinite := by

end QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots

homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries it onto a polygonal (equivalently, piecewise linear or

wild knots, and this is the version formalised here.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Quadrisecant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrisecant)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

def IsKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ γ : Circle → ℝ³, IsEmbedding γ ∧ Set.range γ = K

/-- A *polygonal knot* in `ℝ³`: a knot that is a closed polygon, i.e. the union of the closed
segments `[v i, v (i + 1)]` over a finite cyclic sequence of vertices `v`. -/
def IsPolygonalKnot (P : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=

def IsTameKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsKnot K ∧ ∃ h : ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, IsPolygonalKnot (h '' K)

  IsKnot K ∧ ¬ IsTameKnot K

a set `K ⊆ ℝ³` if it meets `K` in at least four distinct points. -/
def IsQuadrisecant (K : Set ℝ³) (ℓ : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank ℝ ℓ.direction = 1 ∧ 4 ≤ (K ∩ ℓ).encard

@[category API, AMS 51 57]
lemma IsTameKnot.isKnot {K : Set ℝ³} (hK : IsTameKnot K) : IsKnot K :=
  hK.1

@[category API, AMS 51 57]
lemma IsWildKnot.isKnot {K : Set ℝ³} (hK : IsWildKnot K) : IsKnot K :=
  hK.1

/-- A polygonal knot is tame (take the identity homeomorphism). -/
@[category API, AMS 51 57]
lemma IsPolygonalKnot.isTameKnot {P : Set ℝ³} (hP : IsPolygonalKnot P) : IsTameKnot P :=
  ⟨hP.1, Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, by simpa using hP⟩

/-- A knot is either tame or wild, and not both. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 57]
lemma isTameKnot_xor_isWildKnot {K : Set ℝ³} (hK : IsKnot K) :
    Xor' (IsTameKnot K) (IsWildKnot K) := by
  by_cases h : IsTameKnot K
  · exact Or.inl ⟨h, fun h' => h'.2 h⟩
  · exact Or.inr ⟨⟨hK, h⟩, h⟩

/--
**Quadrisecants of wild knots.**
Every wild knot $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ (a topological embedding of the circle that is not
carried to a polygonal knot by any homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$) has infinitely many
quadrisecants, i.e. infinitely many distinct straight lines each meeting $K$ in at least four
distinct points.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem quadrisecants_of_wild_knots (K : Set ℝ³) (hK : IsWildKnot K) :
    {ℓ : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³ | IsQuadrisecant K ℓ}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot table is correct; I only note (as the table itself does) that Kuperberg's original conjecture is for wild arcs, whereas the Wikipedia entry and hence this formalization concern wild knots.
modeling_decisions: Knot = subset of ℝ³ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), via the repo's scoped `ℝ³` notation) equal to the range of a topological embedding `Circle → ℝ³`, following the idiom of Wikipedia/InscribedSquare.lean.

Tame = Kuperberg's definition (arXiv:math/9712205, Def. in §'Arbitrary tame knots and links'): there exists a homeomorphism h : ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³ with h '' K a polygonal knot. Of Kuperberg's three equivalent targets (polynomial / PL / smooth) the PL one was chosen because it is elementary to state faithfully; a 'smooth knot' would require an immersion condition to avoid subtle wild-image issues.

Polygonal knot = a knot that equals ⋃ i : Fin (n+1), segment ℝ (v i) (v (i+1)) for a finite cyclic vertex sequence. Indexing over `Fin (n+1)` (never `ZMod 0 = ℤ`) is essential: an infinite polygonal union could be a wild knot (e.g. Fox–Artin style examples). Since h '' K is automatically a topological circle, requiring only that it be a finite union of segments is equivalent to being a PL knot; the `IsKnot` conjunct in `IsPolygonalKnot` is redundant inside `IsTameKnot` but keeps the definition correct standalone.

Wild = knot that is not tame (IsKnot K ∧ ¬ IsTameKnot K), per the decomposition notes; Kuperberg's original conjecture concerns wild arcs, but the Wikipedia 'wild knots' wording is what was formalized as instructed.

Quadrisecant = an affine subspace ℓ with `Module.finrank ℝ ℓ.direction = 1` (a line) such that `4 ≤ (K ∩ ℓ).encard`, i.e. at least four distinct intersection points (as in the decomposition notes and Kuperberg's 'secant with two middle points'). A line containing a segment of K therefore counts as a quadrisecant (encard = ⊤ ≥ 4); this matches the 'at least four' reading. 'Exactly four' was deliberately not used.
'Infinitely many quadrisecants' = `Set.Infinite` of the set of such lines, lines being `AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³` so distinct elements are distinct lines.
